The primary routing signal is the glycoproteome enrichment/analysis.

scope: HLA class I immuno-affinity purification was performed as described by Demmers et al. In short, HLA class I complexes were immunopurified using 0.5 mg W6/32 antibody coupled to 125 μL protein A/G beads (Santa Cruz) from 25 mg whole cell (WC) lysate.
The analysis was started by enriching all HLA class I molecules from WC lysates by immuno-affinity purification using the pan-HLA class I W6/32 antibody.
subcellular_fraction: analyzing HLA class I complexes from crude plasma and inner membrane-enriched fractions
For the PM and IM fractions, 0.16 mg W6/32 antibody coupled to 40 μL protein A/G beads was used for ∼160 and ∼60 μg input, respectively.

PM fractionation was performed by gentle homogenization in an isotonic environment, in the absence of detergents. Homogenized JY cells were applied to a dextran gradient for phase separation (by differential partitioning) into the PM fraction (low-density top fraction) or IM fraction (high-density bottom layer).

Ontology_SampleSourceAndScope_prompt.notes: The experiment involved immuno-affinity purification of HLA class I complexes from three sources: whole cell lysates, plasma membrane (PM) fractions, and inner membrane (IM) fractions. Since the material analyzed by MS was the result of antibody-capture/affinity purification, the scope is 'purified protein or complex'. The subcellular fraction is identified as membrane/surface based on the PM and IM fractionation.
